steps.sub: Pauli-Z on one qubit -> expectation value in [-1, 1] (Lesson 5)

code:
p = (<Z> + 1) / 2

<Z> = 0.6  ->  p = 1.6/2 = 0.8
  (predict class 1, 80% confidence)

<Z> = -0.2 ->  p = 0.8/2 = 0.4
  (predict class 0)
caption: A simple rescale maps the expectation value into a probability-like value in [0, 1].

code:
L = -[y*log(p) + (1-y)*log(1-p)]

y=1, p=0.8:  L = -log(0.8) = 0.2231
y=1, p=0.4:  L = -log(0.4) = 0.9163

4x larger loss for the worse prediction
caption: Cross-entropy penalizes a confidently wrong-leaning prediction much more heavily.

subtitle: A different QML approach — using the quantum computer only to measure similarity.
